title: The AI Era's Lines of Code? A Case Study on What an Engineer's Token Spend Measures
abstract: arXiv:2611.13396v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Organizations use engineers' token spend to monitor AI adoption, set budgets, and measure productivity, but the metric's relationship with engineering output is unclear. We link five weeks of token usage in coding agents to the commits of 404 engineers at JetBrains, and analyze a company survey of 412 employees. We find that token spend varied mostly between engineers, and which engineers spent the most stayed largely the same over the five weeks. Among weeks with similar commit counts, the 90th percentile of spend was 39 to 240 times the 10th. Within an engineer, doubling spend was associated with about 10% more commits. Available work metrics explained 38% of the variation in spend between engineers and 13% of the week-to-week variation within an engineer. In the survey, respondents in technical roles reported in nearly nine of ten agent evaluations using agents for tasks beyond coding, such as analysis, research, and planning. Token

translated_title: AI时代的代码行数？一项关于工程师Token消耗衡量了什么的案例研究
translated_abstract: 各组织使用工程师的token消耗来监控AI采用情况、设定预算以及衡量生产力，但该指标与工程产出之间的关系尚不明确。我们将JetBrains公司404名工程师在编码智能体中五周的token使用情况与其代码提交记录相关联，并分析了一项针对412名员工的公司调查。我们发现，token消耗的差异主要存在于工程师个体之间，且哪些工程师消耗最多在五周内基本保持稳定。在提交数量相近的几周里，token消耗的第90百分位数达到第10百分位数的39至240倍。就单个工程师而言，token消耗翻倍与提交数量增加约10%相关。可用的工作指标解释了工程师之间token消耗变化的38%，以及工程师个体内部周与周之间变化的13%。在调查中，技术岗位的受访者表示，在近九成的智能体使用评估中，他们将智能体用于编码之外的任务，例如分析、研究和规划。
tldr: 研究发现工程师的token消耗主要由个体差异而非工作产出决定，其与代码提交量仅呈弱关联（消耗翻倍仅带来约10%的提交增长），因此token消耗并不是衡量工程生产力的可靠指标。
en_tdlr: A case study at JetBrains shows that engineers' token spend in AI coding agents is driven mostly by individual differences rather than output, correlating only weakly with commit counts (doubling spend yields ~10% more commits), making it a poor proxy for engineering productivity.
